title: Audit, handover and quality improvement
audience: Cleaners and cleaning supervisors who complete work records, handovers and audit checks in residential aged care, clinics, dental practices and NDIS settings in any Australian state or territory.
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: NDIS Practice Standards and Quality Indicators, Version 4 (November 2021), Core Module (cover date November 2021; no page date shown); Aged Care Quality Standards, Action 3.17 (guidance resource): reprocessing reusable equipment and devices ('Last updated' label with no date). Only part of these sources has been confirmed.
learningOutcomes: Complete a traceable task record that shows what was cleaned, how, when and by whom, without claiming clinical sterility or certification.
Describe a supervisor observation and a handover that lets the next person act without asking the cleaner.
Record a missed area or a variance honestly and arrange a safe correction under the approved procedure.
Identify a quality improvement point from audit findings and pass it to the responsible person.

instruction.heading: What an audit is for
instruction.body: An audit checks whether the work was done as the schedule and instruction require, and whether the controls are working. In residential aged care, clinics and NDIS settings an audit may be a supervisor walk-through, a checklist against the schedule, a review of the work records, or an external inspection. The NDIS Practice Standards, Version 4 of November 2021, require that the risk management system includes, where relevant, measures to prevent and control infections. The Aged Care Quality Standards Action 3.17 guidance resource (no date shown) refers to traceability of reprocessed items, which depends on accurate records. An audit only helps the facility if the record is honest. A record that says a task was complete when it was not defeats the purpose of the audit.

instruction.heading: A complete task record
instruction.body: A complete record shows the area or item, the date and time, the schedule or instruction followed, the product and method used, the frequency, the surfaces covered, any exception, the person who did the work and the handover. Write the record at the time of the task. Do not describe a result in terms that suggest clinical sterility, certification or a disinfection that was not achieved. A cleaner records what was done, not what the facility would like to be true. Where a field cannot be completed, leave a clear note rather than a guess.

instruction.heading: Variance, missed areas and honest correction
instruction.body: A variance is any difference between the schedule or instruction and what was done. A missed area is a surface or room on the schedule that was not cleaned. When you find a missed area, or an audit finds one, record it as found, not as already fixed. Arrange a correction under the approved procedure, such as cleaning the area now, and record the correction with the time. If the correction cannot be done safely or in time, tell the supervisor and record the postponement. Do not reopen a record to hide a gap, and do not add a completion time that was not observed.

instruction.heading: Handover that works
instruction.body: A handover tells the next person what is done, what is not done, what is blocked and who must be contacted. Keep it short and factual: the area, the status, any stop or referral, any product shortfall, any resident request, and the next step. Handover to the supervisor or the next shift in the way the facility requires. Do not assume that the next person knows about a restriction or a stop. If an area is restricted, the handover must say so, and the restriction notice must stay in place until the responsible person removes it.

instruction.heading: Quality improvement from audit findings
instruction.body: A repeated finding is a signal that the system needs attention, not only that one cleaner made a mistake. If the same surface is missed each week, the schedule, the route or the workload may need review. Pass the finding to your supervisor in writing, with the evidence and the pattern you observed, and suggest a change for the responsible person to consider. Do not change the schedule yourself. The improvement is made by the facility, and your role is to make the problem visible and accurately recorded.

procedure: Complete the task record at the time of work, with the area, time, schedule or instruction, product, method, frequency and person.
Record any exception, variance or missed area as found, and do not describe it as already corrected unless it has been corrected and the time recorded.
Arrange any correction under the approved procedure, and record the correction and the time.
Prepare the handover for the next person with the status, any stop or referral, any product shortfall, and the next step.
During an audit, present the record honestly and answer the questions asked, without changing the record afterwards.
Pass repeated findings or quality concerns to the supervisor in writing with the evidence.

workedExamples.situation: A supervisor walks the unit and finds a handrail on the schedule that has no record of cleaning for the day. Your record for the day says the unit was complete.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not add a completion entry for a time that was not observed. Record the handrail as a missed area, clean it now under the approved procedure if it is safe to do so, and record the correction with the time. Tell the supervisor and let the record show the gap and the correction. An honest record protects the residents and the facility.

workedExamples.situation: At handover, a room is restricted by a notice that you put on the door after an unexplained change in the resident's condition. The incoming cleaner does not know about the notice.
workedExamples.reasoning: The handover must say the room is restricted, give the notice, and name the person who confirmed the restriction. Do not assume the next person knows. Keep the notice in place until the responsible person removes it in writing, and record the handover with the time.

equipmentAndPpe: Task record or electronic record in the form the facility uses
Schedule, instruction and audit checklist for the area
Handover sheet or the facility's handover system

commonErrors.error: Recording a completed task at the end of the shift from memory, with times that were not observed.
commonErrors.prevention: Record at the time of the task. Never add a completion time that was not observed.

commonErrors.error: Reopening a record to hide a missed area after an audit has found it.
commonErrors.prevention: Record the miss as found, correct it, and record the correction with its time.

commonErrors.error: Handing over without mentioning a restriction, stop or product shortfall.
commonErrors.prevention: Include every stop, referral, restriction and shortfall in the handover.

commonErrors.error: Treating a repeated finding as one person's error and not reporting the pattern.
commonErrors.prevention: Report repeated findings to the supervisor in writing with the evidence.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The NDIS Practice Standards, Version 4 of November 2021, Core Module, require that the risk management system includes, where relevant, measures to prevent and control infections and outbreaks, and that incidents involving infectious material are reported, recorded, investigated and reviewed.

The Aged Care Quality Standards Action 3.17 guidance resource (no date shown) covers reprocessing reusable equipment and devices, including traceability, storage and transport, and workforce training. Reprocessing is outside this course.
Licence notice: Completing a task record or an audit does not grant any licence, accreditation or certification.

qualityStandard: The learner completes a supplied task record with every required field, recorded at the time of the task.
The learner records a supplied missed area as found, and then records the correction with its time.
The learner prepares a handover for a supplied area that includes a restriction, a stop and a product shortfall.
The learner passes a repeated finding to the supervisor in writing with the evidence and the pattern.
documentationEvidence: Complete task record with area, time, schedule or instruction, product, method and person
Missed area or variance as found, with the correction and its time
Handover record with status, stops, restrictions and shortfalls
summary: A record is an honest statement of what was done, at the time it was done.
A missed area is recorded as found. The correction is recorded separately with its own time.
A handover includes every stop, restriction and shortfall, and does not assume the next person knows.
Repeated findings are passed to the responsible person as a pattern, not hidden or fixed by changing the schedule.

knowledgeChecks.question: An audit finds a handrail on the schedule with no record of cleaning. What is the correct record?
options: Add a completion time for the handrail so the record is complete for the audit today
Record the handrail as a missed area as found, then record the correction with its own time.
Remove the handrail from the schedule so the record is complete and nothing looks missed

knowledgeChecks.question: What must a handover include for a room that has a restriction notice on the door?
options: Nothing, because the notice is on the door for everyone to see and read as they pass
Only the time the room was last cleaned and the name of the cleaner on the day
The restriction, the notice, and the person who confirmed it, so the next person knows.

knowledgeChecks.question: A cleaner notices the same surface is missed every week. What should they do?
options: Report the repeated finding to the supervisor in writing with the evidence, and do not change the schedule.
Clean it in secret each week so no one notices the gap in the schedule at all, and the record stays tidy
Change the schedule so the surface is cleaned on a different day, which should solve the problem for everyone
